properties.name: BART Silicon Valley Phase II
properties.headline: Bay Area Rapid Transit (BART) from Berryessa through downtown San José to Santa Clara
properties.statusReason: Shown as funded because major construction is under way: the tunnel launch pit was finished in September 2026. The money is not all in place. About $564 million of the $12.7 billion cost has no source yet, and the $5.1 billion federal share is not guaranteed until a grant agreement is signed, expected in late 2027.
properties.summary: Bay Area Rapid Transit (BART) trains would extend six miles from the Berryessa/North San José station through downtown San José to Santa Clara, with four BART stations: new underground stations at 28th Street/Little Portugal and Downtown San José, new underground platforms at the existing Diridon Station, and a ground level stop beside the Caltrain station at Santa Clara. Most of the line runs underground in one large tunnel.

cost.note: The May 2026 report from the Santa Clara Valley Transportation Authority (VTA) lists a current estimate of $12,714.5 million, against an original baseline of $12,746 million. VTA is preparing a new cost estimate, so the figure may change.

opening.note: This is the target of the Santa Clara Valley Transportation Authority for starting passenger service (second quarter of 2037). The Federal Transit Administration risk review points to early 2039, and the agency is rebuilding its schedule.

sources.title: VTA BART Silicon Valley Phase II monthly report, May 2026
VTA fact sheet, BART Silicon Valley Phase II, May 2026
VTA BART Silicon Valley program website
VTA BART Silicon Valley Phase II fall newsletter

properties.name: Eastridge to BART Regional Connector
properties.headline: Light rail extension along Capitol Expressway to Eastridge
properties.statusReason: Major construction is well under way and the transit agency reports the project 67 percent complete as of May 31, 2026.
properties.summary: This extends Santa Clara Valley Transportation Authority (VTA) light rail 2.4 miles from the existing Alum Rock station along Capitol Expressway in San José to a new Eastridge station. Two new stations are planned, an elevated one at Story Road and one at ground level at the Eastridge Transit Center. Riders there could then connect to Bay Area Rapid Transit (BART) at the Milpitas station.

cost.note: Latest figure found, from a July 2025 notice to the board of the Santa Clara Valley Transportation Authority. No newer official figure was found.

opening.note: Construction is expected to finish in late 2027, then testing and safety certification come before passengers ride. The agency has moved this date later more than once.

sources.title: VTA project page, Eastridge to BART Regional Connector
VTA Eastridge project newsletter, summer 2026
VTA board correspondence, July 2025

properties.name: Geary Boulevard Improvement Project
properties.headline: Bus stop and safety upgrades along the Geary bus lanes in the Richmond
properties.statusReason: The $17.6 million contract for the remaining street work was awarded in July 2026 with its funding sources named, and work is due to start in fall 2026. Bus lanes from a first phase have been in place since 2023. The agency puts the whole project at about $48 million.
properties.summary: Bus lanes were added between 34th Avenue and Stanyan Street in a quick first phase in 2023; this phase adds sidewalk extensions at bus stops and crossings, new traffic signals and repaving. The San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency says the project aims to improve service on the 38 Geary and 38R Geary Rapid bus lines and make walking safer.

cost.note: About $48 million for the project as listed on the agency page.

opening.note: Predicted completion date on the agency page.

sources.title: SFMTA: Geary Boulevard Improvement Project
San Francisco Public Works Commission award report, July 23, 2026

properties.name: Mission Bay Ferry Landing
properties.headline: New ferry dock in Mission Bay, San Francisco
properties.statusReason: The construction contract was awarded in 2026 within a $41 million budget approved by the Port Commission, with funding from Port, city, regional and federal sources. Only the landing is funded; no ferry route, start date or money to run service has been announced.
properties.summary: The Port of San Francisco and the Water Emergency Transportation Authority (WETA) are building a ferry landing at Agua Vista Park in Mission Bay with a covered pier, gangway and electric charging equipment. The landing gives ferries a dock near UCSF (University of California, San Francisco) hospitals and Chase Center.

cost.note: Not to exceed budget for the construction phase authorized June 9, 2026. The winning bid was $33.0 million. Covers the final construction phase only. Earlier dredging and demolition phases and the floating dock supplied by the ferry agency are not included.

opening.note: No date has been set for ferry service to start. Building the landing is scheduled to finish in March 2028.

sources.title: Port of San Francisco: Mission Bay Ferry Landing
San Francisco Public Works Commission resolution awarding the construction contract
San Francisco Public Works Commission staff report, July 23, 2026

properties.name: SMART Healdsburg Extension
properties.headline: Sonoma-Marin Area Rail Transit (SMART) trains extended from Windsor to Healdsburg
properties.statusReason: SMART (Sonoma-Marin Area Rail Transit) and the California Transportation Commission both say the extension is fully funded through construction; main construction starts in 2027.
properties.summary: Sonoma-Marin Area Rail Transit (SMART) will add about nine miles of track north from Windsor to a new station in Healdsburg, plus an extension of the walking and cycling path beside the tracks. Riders in Healdsburg could then take the train to Santa Rosa, Petaluma, San Rafael and Larkspur. SMART has not yet chosen the station site: near the historic depot on Hudson Street, or downtown near Vine Street.

cost.note: California Transportation Commission, January 2026, which says the project is fully funded through construction.

opening.note: SMART (Sonoma-Marin Area Rail Transit) lists construction from January 2027, testing in November and December 2028, and service beginning in December 2028.

sources.title: Sonoma-Marin Area Rail Transit: Healdsburg extension project page
California Transportation Commission: Healdsburg Extension memo, Resolution E-26-08A (January 2026)
Sonoma-Marin Area Rail Transit: earlier funding announcement (July 2023)
Sonoma-Marin Area Rail Transit: Healdsburg station location page

properties.name: Transbay Corridor Core Capacity Program
properties.headline: More trains through the Transbay Tube under the Bay, with new train control
properties.statusReason: The $2.7 billion core project has its full funding committed under a federal grant agreement signed in September 2020, and construction is under way. About $100 million of the wider $4.44 billion program is not yet secured.
properties.summary: Bay Area Rapid Transit (BART) is replacing its aging train control system with a modern computer based one, adding railcars, building a storage yard at the Hayward Maintenance Complex and adding power substations. Today up to 24 trains an hour can run each way through the Transbay Tube between Oakland and San Francisco. The goal is 28 by 2030 and later 30. The work is systemwide, so the map shows one marker.

cost.note: BART's September 2026 estimate for the whole program, including 306 new railcars; about $100 million was not yet secured. The project in the 2020 federal agreement was $2.7 billion, including a $1.17 billion federal grant.

opening.note: The BART page also states a longer term goal of up to 30 trains per hour and gives no completion date for the train control rollout, so 2030 applies only to the 28 trains per hour target.

sources.title: BART Core Capacity project page
BART quarterly capital program report, fiscal year 2026 Q4

properties.name: Berkeley Pier and Ferry Terminal
properties.headline: Proposed ferry route between Berkeley and San Francisco
properties.statusReason: About $11 million is secured for design and environmental review. No money has been found to build the $105.8 million project. The City has asked the Metropolitan Transportation Commission for up to $25 million for work on land.
properties.summary: The City of Berkeley and the Water Emergency Transportation Authority (WETA) want to rebuild the closed Berkeley Municipal Pier as a 1,080-foot pier with a ferry terminal, a breakwater and charging for electric boats. It would open a new Berkeley to San Francisco ferry route, projected to carry over 1,000 passengers on an average weekday. The pier would stay open to people fishing and walking.

leadAgency.name: City of Berkeley, with the Water Emergency Transportation Authority (WETA) as partner

cost.note: City of Berkeley construction cost estimate based on designs that are 60 percent complete, September 2026.

opening.note: No opening date has been published.

sources.title: San Francisco Bay Ferry: Berkeley Ferry Project
Berkeley Pier and Ferry Terminal Project Fact Sheet (June 25, 2026)
City of Berkeley: Pier Ferry Access Project
City of Berkeley Council item (September 15, 2026): grant application, Safe Routes to Transit and Bay Trail

properties.name: Burlingame Broadway Grade Separation Project
properties.headline: Plan to raise Caltrain above Broadway in Burlingame and close the Broadway stop
properties.statusReason: Design is 65 percent complete and Caltrain says funding gaps remain for the $662 million project. The Federal Railroad Administration awarded $90 million toward construction in November 2026; construction could start in November 2028 only if the rest is found.
properties.summary: Caltrain tracks cross Broadway in Burlingame at street level. The project would raise the tracks so trains no longer cross the road, and add pedestrian underpasses at Cadillac Way and Sanchez Avenue. This is called a grade separation. The existing Broadway station would close permanently, and the Burlingame City Council agreed in March 2025 to proceed without a rebuilt Broadway station.

cost.note: Total including design, property, utilities and construction.

opening.note: No opening date is published. Construction could begin as soon as November 2028, subject to funding.

sources.title: Caltrain: Burlingame Broadway Grade Separation Project
Caltrain: federal investment in Caltrain corridor grade separation funding
Caltrain: Broadway grade separation design update

properties.name: California High-Speed Rail in the Bay Area
properties.headline: Planned high-speed trains from San Francisco through San José to Gilroy
properties.statusReason: No construction money is committed for the Bay Area part: state law limits the California High-Speed Rail Authority to spending on the Merced to Bakersfield section in the Central Valley, and Bay Area work has not started.
properties.summary: The California High-Speed Rail Authority plans high-speed trains that share upgraded Caltrain tracks from San Francisco to San José, then use an upgraded freight line to Gilroy and continue toward the Central Valley. The map draws only the Bay Area part, from San Francisco to Gilroy. The Central Valley link east of Gilroy is not drawn.

cost.note: The California High-Speed Rail Authority's 2026 Business Plan lists $1.3 billion for San Francisco to Gilroy work but leaves out a $2 billion to $5 billion upgrade of the San José to Gilroy line, so there is no full Bay Area cost. San Francisco to Bakersfield is put at $61.2 billion.

opening.note: The California High-Speed Rail Authority's 2026 Business Plan targets 2039 for San Francisco to Bakersfield service. This is a target, not a funded schedule.

sources.title: California High-Speed Rail Authority 2026 Business Plan (June 2026)

properties.name: Capitol Corridor South Bay Connect
properties.headline: Proposed Capitol Corridor reroute along the Bay with a new Fremont station
properties.statusReason: As of March 2025, about $183 million of the estimated $990 million was secured, and construction is not expected to start before mid 2029.
properties.summary: South Bay Connect would move Capitol Corridor trains between Oakland Coliseum and Newark from the inland Niles route onto an existing freight line closer to the Bay. A new Fremont station at the Ardenwood Park-and-Ride would add connections toward the Peninsula, and riders would save about 13 minutes each way. Trains would no longer stop at the Hayward and Fremont Centerville stations; Altamont Corridor Express (ACE) trains would still stop in Fremont. It adds no trains.

cost.note: California Transportation Commission estimate, March 2025.

opening.note: No opening date. State environmental review was certified in November 2024; construction is estimated to begin between mid 2029 and mid 2030, depending on funding.

sources.title: South Bay Connect project website
South Bay Connect fact sheet, June 2024
California Transportation Commission item, March 2025
City of Hayward news item, November 2024
South Bay Connect frequently asked questions, June 2024

properties.name: Central Subway North Beach Extension Study
properties.headline: Study of extending the Muni T Third subway one stop to North Beach
properties.statusReason: This is only a study that runs from mid 2026 to mid 2028; no design, construction funding or cost estimate exists.
properties.summary: The Central Subway runs the Muni T Third line underground from South of Market to Chinatown. The San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency is studying a one station extension to North Beach, using unfinished tunnels that already end near Columbus Avenue and Union Street. It is also looking at a longer extension toward Fisherman's Wharf. Station locations and the exact route are not decided.

cost.note: No official cost estimate has been published. The study is meant to produce a rough estimate.

opening.note: No opening date has been set. The study itself is planned to finish by mid 2028.

sources.title: SFMTA: Central Subway Extension

properties.name: Diridon Station Redevelopment
properties.headline: Plan for a rebuilt, larger Diridon Station in San José
properties.statusReason: Only the environmental review is funded, with $41 million approved over three years; no construction funding or construction cost estimate has been published.
properties.summary: Diridon Station in San José would be expanded and redesigned. It would serve Caltrain, Altamont Corridor Express (ACE), Capitol Corridor, Amtrak and Santa Clara Valley Transportation Authority (VTA) buses and light rail, and later Bay Area Rapid Transit (BART) and high-speed rail. The recommended design keeps the tracks at ground level. Street crossings at Park Avenue, San Carlos Street, Auzerais Avenue and West Virginia Street would also change.

leadAgency.name: City of San José, Caltrain, Santa Clara Valley Transportation Authority (VTA) and two other agencies

cost.note: No official cost estimate for building the station has been published. The $41 million approved so far pays for environmental review and planning only.

opening.note: No opening date has been set. The project is still in environmental review.

sources.title: Diridon Station project website
Caltrain board packet, September 3, 2026 (Diridon update)

properties.name: Geary / 19th Avenue Subway
properties.headline: Proposed subway from downtown San Francisco through the Richmond and Sunset to Daly City
properties.statusReason: Only a first planning study is finished; the report says current funding sources cannot pay for the project and no construction money has been identified.
properties.summary: The San Francisco County Transportation Authority studied a subway about 10 miles long with five or six stations, from near the Salesforce Transit Center west under Geary Boulevard, then south under 19th Avenue to near Daly City BART (Bay Area Rapid Transit). The technology (BART, regional rail, Muni Metro light rail or automated light rail) and route are not chosen; the line on the map only shows the corridor being studied.

cost.note: A planning level range in 2026 dollars that leaves out some costs such as land and financing.

opening.note: No opening date has been set. The report notes that big transit projects typically take 15 to 20 years from start to service.

sources.title: SFCTA: Geary/19th Ave Subway and Regional Connections Study, strategic case report
SFCTA: project page

properties.name: Irvington BART Station
properties.headline: Proposed Bay Area Rapid Transit (BART) station in Fremont's Irvington district
properties.statusReason: About $122 million of an estimated $282 million is secured; the rest is not, BART wants a new cost estimate before seeking more money, and federal environmental approval is still needed for federal grants.
properties.summary: This would be a new Bay Area Rapid Transit (BART) station in Fremont's Irvington district, near Osgood Road and Washington Boulevard, on the existing line between Fremont and Warm Springs/South Fremont stations. BART says design is less than 80 percent complete and the City of Fremont has bought most of the land, but construction cannot start without the rest of the funding.

leadAgency.name: City of Fremont (project sponsor) and Bay Area Rapid Transit (BART)

cost.note: A 2021 estimate cited by BART in January 2026. The cost items in a 2025 Alameda County Transportation Commission fact sheet add up to about $289.5 million. BART recommends a new independent estimate, so this figure is out of date.

opening.note: No opening date is set. An earlier City of Fremont date of 2031 depends on funding that has not been secured.

sources.title: BART letter to Senator Wahab, January 28, 2026
Alameda County Transportation Commission fact sheet, spring 2025

properties.name: Link21
properties.headline: Proposed second rail crossing under San Francisco Bay
properties.statusReason: Link21 is still in early planning with no chosen route or total cost, and only planning money (about $200 million from Bay Area Rapid Transit and the Metropolitan Transportation Commission) is identified.
properties.summary: Link21 is a joint program of Bay Area Rapid Transit (BART) and the Capitol Corridor Joint Powers Authority, which has run it day to day since 2025. It would build a new underground rail crossing of San Francisco Bay between Oakland and San Francisco. The agencies have chosen regional trains like Caltrain for it, not BART trains, but the route, stations and schedule are not decided. The map point is only a marker in the Bay.

leadAgency.name: Capitol Corridor Joint Powers Authority (manages the program, with BART as a partner)

cost.note: No official cost estimate has been published.

opening.note: No opening date has been set; the program has not yet reached environmental review.

sources.title: Link21 program home page
Link21 current planning activities
Link21 financial information
Capitol Corridor press release, June 19, 2025

properties.name: Muni Metro Train Control Upgrade Project
properties.headline: Plan for new computer train control on the Muni Metro light rail lines
properties.statusReason: Phase 1 ($155 million) has state, federal and local money set aside and is being designed, but no official source shows how the full $700 million program would be paid for. The train control supplier, Hitachi Rail, was hired in January 2025. A state document aims to award the Phase 1 building contract in June 2027.
properties.summary: The San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency plans to replace a train control system built on 1980s technology and installed in the Market Street subway in 1998. Work would start on the surface along the Embarcadero and Third Street, then move into the subway and the J, K, L, M, N and T lines. The agency says it would add about 20 percent more capacity, with up to 40 trains an hour in the Market Street subway.

cost.note: Total for all seven phases, from the California Transportation Commission baseline document (December 2025 meeting).

opening.note: The agency's target for finishing all seven phases. No funding plan for the full program has been published, so this date could change. A December 2025 state document schedules Phase 1 from November 2026 to July 2028.

sources.title: SFMTA: Train Control Upgrade Project
California Transportation Commission baseline agreement, Phase 1, December 2025
SFMTA: partnership with Hitachi Rail

properties.name: Redwood City Ferry Terminal
properties.headline: Proposed ferry terminal at the Port of Redwood City
properties.statusReason: Design and environmental review are under way; no official source shows a full funding plan for building the terminal or running the service.
properties.summary: The Port of Redwood City and the Water Emergency Transportation Authority (WETA) are studying and designing a ferry terminal at the port to connect Redwood City and nearby Peninsula communities with Oakland and San Francisco. In 2024 they ran four trial Sunday ferries to Giants games to test interest. No regular service has been scheduled.

leadAgency.name: Port of Redwood City, with the Water Emergency Transportation Authority (WETA)

cost.note: No official cost estimate has been published on the pages reviewed.

opening.note: No opening date has been published.

sources.title: San Francisco Bay Ferry: Redwood City Ferry Project
San Francisco Bay Ferry: REEF (Rapid Electric Emission Free) program page
Port of Redwood City: Ferry Terminal Project

properties.name: Regional Mapping and Wayfinding Project
properties.headline: Plan for one set of maps and signs for all Bay Area transit
properties.statusReason: The Metropolitan Transportation Commission (MTC) has hired companies to make signs for nine pilot hubs and some bus stops, but there is no money yet for the whole region. A regional transit sales tax that is ahead in early, unofficial November 2026 results could pay for it in five counties. MTC has not set an amount.
properties.summary: The Metropolitan Transportation Commission (MTC) is creating one design for transit maps, signs and screens so buses, trains and ferries across all nine counties look and read the same. The first installations are planned at nine hubs, including the Larkspur Ferry and Sonoma-Marin Area Rail Transit (SMART) station, plus selected bus stops in Sonoma and Solano counties. This is part of the Transit Transformation Action Plan (a regional plan to make transit easier to use).

cost.note: No official total cost has been published on the pages reviewed.

opening.note: The Metropolitan Transportation Commission (MTC) says the pilot delivery schedule is still to be set.

sources.title: MTC: Regional Mapping and Wayfinding
MTC news: MTC Picks Vendors for New, Improved Signs (June 12, 2026)
Metropolitan Transportation Commission: Regional Transit Measure (Senate Bill 63)
MTC: Senate Bill 63 rider-focused improvements expenditure plan

properties.name: Reimagine Dumbarton
properties.headline: Proposed busway and trail on the old Dumbarton rail line, Redwood City to East Palo Alto
properties.statusReason: This is still a study. SamTrans (San Mateo County Transit District) has money only for environmental review and early engineering, and no money to build it has been found.
properties.summary: SamTrans (San Mateo County Transit District) is studying a dedicated busway with nine new bus stations on the former Dumbarton freight rail corridor between University Avenue in East Palo Alto and Middlefield Road in Redwood City, plus a wide paved trail. It replaces earlier plans for passenger trains on the corridor. A preferred design is due to be selected, and construction would not start until after 2031.

cost.note: No official cost estimate has been published for the busway.

opening.note: No opening date has been set. SamTrans says construction would be after 2031, pending funding.

sources.title: SamTrans: Reimagine Dumbarton

properties.name: San Pablo Avenue Bus Lanes and Bike Lanes Project
properties.headline: Proposed bus only lanes and protected bike lanes on San Pablo Avenue, Oakland to Berkeley
properties.statusReason: Only about $8.3 million of the estimated $258.5 million is secured, and the project is still in preliminary design and environmental review.
properties.summary: This project would turn one traffic lane in each direction on San Pablo Avenue into a bus only lane and replace parking lanes with protected bike lanes. It covers 3.5 miles from 16th Street in downtown Oakland through Emeryville to Heinz Avenue in South Berkeley, and also adds safer crossings and bus stop improvements. Buses should be faster and more reliable, and parking and loading would move to side streets.

cost.note: Total cost estimate in the April 2026 project fact sheet, of which about $8.3 million (Measure BB (Alameda County's transportation sales tax) and regional funds) is secured and $250.2 million is not yet identified.

opening.note: No opening or completion year is stated. The fact sheet gives only a construction window of spring 2032 to spring 2034.

sources.title: Alameda CTC San Pablo Avenue project page
San Pablo Avenue Bus Lanes and Bike Lanes capital project fact sheet

properties.name: SMART Cloverdale Extension and Geyserville Station
properties.headline: Proposed extension of Sonoma-Marin Area Rail Transit (SMART) trains north to Cloverdale
properties.statusReason: Sonoma-Marin Area Rail Transit (SMART) says the Cloverdale extension is not yet fully funded and it is still seeking state and federal grants.
properties.summary: Sonoma-Marin Area Rail Transit (SMART) plans to continue the line about 18 miles north from Healdsburg to Cloverdale, with a station at Geyserville near Highway 128 and Remmel Road. On August 19, 2026 SMART staff asked its Board to adopt the Geyserville station project. Money to build the station and the extension has not been secured.

cost.note: No official cost estimate for the Healdsburg to Cloverdale section has been found on pages of SMART (Sonoma-Marin Area Rail Transit).

opening.note: No opening date has been set because construction money has not been secured.

sources.title: Sonoma-Marin Area Rail Transit: Geyserville station page
Sonoma-Marin Area Rail Transit: Healdsburg extension page (FAQ)
Sonoma-Marin Area Rail Transit: August 19, 2026 staff report on the Geyserville station

properties.name: The Portal (Transbay Downtown Rail Extension)
properties.headline: Plan to extend Caltrain underground from Fourth and King to the Salesforce Transit Center
properties.statusReason: The federal government promised $3.38 billion in 2024, and the state awarded $750 million in November 2026. The final federal grant contract is not expected before July 2027, and a federal review found a large funding gap.
properties.summary: The Portal would extend Caltrain 2.2 miles underground from its current end at Fourth and King Streets to the Salesforce Transit Center in downtown San Francisco, with a new underground station at Fourth and Townsend Streets. Caltrain riders could then get off in the downtown financial district instead of at the edge of South of Market. The tunnel is also meant to carry California high-speed rail trains.

leadAgency.name: Transbay Joint Powers Authority (the agency that built the Salesforce Transit Center)

cost.note: Cost accepted in the 2023 federal review, in dollars of the years the money is spent. The agency proposes $7.57 billion, the figure the state used for its 2026 award; federal review of the lower figure was not finished in July 2026.

opening.note: Depends on funding. The Transbay Joint Powers Authority website still says 2035.

properties.name: Treasure Island Electric Ferry Service
properties.headline: Plan for an electric San Francisco Bay Ferry boat on the Treasure Island route
properties.statusReason: Most of the $110.4 million equipment and terminal cost has named funding sources, but regional money is still awaiting approval and the 10-year operating budget has a gap of $0.3 million to $2.3 million.
properties.summary: The Water Emergency Transportation Authority (WETA) plans to run a public ferry between Treasure Island and the San Francisco Ferry Building using one battery electric boat that carries 150 passengers and 25 bicycles, with up to 15 round trips a day. A ferry already runs on this route, provided by the island's developer as an interim service; this project would replace it with WETA service on a new battery electric boat. The proposed $5 fare matches today's fare.

cost.note: Capital cost in dollars of the years the money is spent, as presented to the Treasure Island Mobility Management Agency committee on June 16, 2026. It includes the $61.0 million terminal the developer has already built and uses today, the electric boat and a spare boat, and charging equipment. A business plan is still being finished, so the figure may change.

opening.text: Mid to late 2027 (target, depends on funding)
opening.note: The June 2026 presentation anticipates a start in mid to late 2027, once all equipment is available, with service launching in fiscal year 2027/28. The plan notes the service level is pending funding.

sources.title: San Francisco County Transportation Authority: Treasure Island Ferry Business Plan Update (June 16, 2026)
San Francisco Bay Ferry: REEF (Rapid Electric Emission Free) program
San Francisco Bay Ferry: Treasure Island Ferry Service
Treasure Island Mobility Management Agency committee memo (July 8, 2025): ferry terminal contract

properties.name: Valley Link Rail, Phase 1A
properties.headline: Proposed rail line from the Dublin/Pleasanton train station to Livermore
properties.statusReason: About $669 million is committed, but the agency's own funding plan of about $2.04 billion still depends on roughly $1.38 billion that is hoped for from grants not yet awarded, and construction has not started.
properties.summary: Valley Link is a planned passenger rail line that would link Bay Area Rapid Transit (BART) with the San Joaquin Valley. Phase 1A is about 11 miles, mostly in the middle of Interstate 580, from Dublin/Pleasanton BART to Vasco Road in Livermore, where riders could change to Altamont Corridor Express (ACE) trains. It has three stations and battery electric trains. The extension toward Mountain House (Phase 1B) has no funding plan yet.

leadAgency.name: Tri-Valley San Joaquin Valley Regional Rail Authority (Valley Link)

cost.note: This is the authority's August 2026 estimate in dollars of the years the money is spent ($2,025 million to $2,186 million). It leaves out the trains, which the authority plans to lease. The same document's funding plan totals about $2.04 billion in 2024 dollars.

opening.note: No opening date has been officially published for Phase 1A; the project is still in early design and the authority aims to ask the Federal Transit Administration in December 2026 to move to its next grant stage.

sources.title: Valley Link project page
Valley Link Phase 1A industry outreach presentation (August 2026)
Valley Link news releases

properties.name: VTA Visionary Network and 2027 Service Plan
properties.headline: Plan for more frequent weekend buses and light rail across Santa Clara County
properties.statusReason: The Santa Clara Valley Transportation Authority (VTA) Board approved the 2027 plan on October 1, 2026, but the extra weekend service needs new money to run. Early results show a regional transit sales tax passing on November 3, 2026, but they are not final, and no official source yet ties that money to this plan.
properties.summary: The Santa Clara Valley Transportation Authority (VTA) has a long-term plan adopted by its Board, the Visionary Network, for more frequent bus and light rail service across the county. Its first phase, for 2027, would run 12 frequent bus routes and the Blue, Green and Orange light rail lines every 15 minutes on weekends. It needs new operating money. The plan adds no new Rapid lines (Rapid lines are frequent buses that make fewer stops), only new stops on Rapid 500 and 522.

cost.note: The transit agency's project pages do not state a cost for the first phase.

opening.note: The first phase would start during 2027 only if new transit operating money becomes available. No start date has been set.

sources.title: VTA 2027 Transit Service Plan page
VTA Visionary Network page
Metropolitan Transportation Commission: Regional Transit Measure (Senate Bill 63)
